# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 40 (Bi-Vb Pc40)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc40  
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 40  
**Title (English, from literature):** Not wandering after the rainy season  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 40, titled *Cārikanapakkamana* ("Not wandering after the rainy season"), stipulates that a nun who does not set out wandering after the rainy season residence must confess an offense. In the origin story preserved in the Vibhaṅga, laypeople complained that the nuns remained in one location and became a burden to the community rather than moving on [Hüsken 1997]. As Ute Hüsken observes, this rule was formulated specifically for nuns, who faced far stricter travel restrictions than monks—including prohibitions against travelling alone or travelling without a caravan through dangerous territory—which may have led them to settle in one settlement for extended periods [Hüsken 1997].

By the time of the Pali commentary, the *Samantapāsādikā*, this legal requirement had evolved into a formality: the commentary notes that it was sufficient for nuns merely to walk a designated minimum distance before returning to their original starting point [Hüsken 1997]. Modern translations of the rule include an English translation by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
